claim_summary: TimeSeriesGym contributes a scalable, agent-agnostic benchmark environment with diverse time-series ML engineering challenges and artifact-specific evaluation.

claim_evidence.quote: We propose TimeSeriesGym, the first open source benchmark environment for evaluating AI agents on time series ML engineering tasks (Fig. 1).
TimeSeriesGym provides a comprehensive framework that evaluates multimodal agent outputs (e.g., prediction files, models, code) across specific ML skills

modules.name: Time-series challenge benchmark and artifact grading
modules.scope_reason: The contribution packages challenges, resources and graders around agents. R3_1_TSK is no because it does not provide a single task-family procedure; changing challenge family changes the challenge-specific grader, not the benchmark runtime. R3_2_GTS is no because the environment itself does not implement shared temporal-order, window, frequency or availability logic. R3_3_GH applies to the general execution/evaluation environment.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - challenge platform covers multiple objectives; per-challenge criteria are not a reusable task procedure
R3_2_GTS:no - no shared temporal semantics in the platform mechanism
R3_3_GH:yes - environment packages resources, execution and grading

evidence.quote: Each challenge in TimeSeriesGym is organized with a consistent structure: (1) resources including datasets, code repositories, related paper(s) and documentation relevant to the challenge; (2) a description file that outlines the challenge parameters, available resources, and provides specific instructions and hints for successful completion; and (3) challenge-specific grading functions to evaluate agent submissions.

Our evaluation methodology deliberately combines multiple assessment approaches: quantitative metrics (accuracy, mean absolute error), programmatic analysis (regular expression matching, code inspection), and qualitative evaluation (LLM-as-a-judge) (see Appendix E).

process_validity.quote: the percentage of challenges where the agent made a (1) valid, and (2) reasonable submission. A submission is valid if the grader returns any non-null score.

task_performance.quote: We report the raw scores achieved by each agent on every challenge (Tab 3).
